name: Hemoglobin
notes: Lower in pregnancy (~11 g/dL acceptable). Decreased in anemia, increased in polycythemia.

name: Hematocrit
notes: Rule of three: Hct ≈ 3 × Hgb.

name: Red Blood Cell Count
notes: Decreased in anemia; elevated in polycythemia vera.

name: White Blood Cell Count
notes: Leukocytosis (>11,000): infection, inflammation, leukemia. Leukopenia (<4,500): viral infection, marrow suppression.

name: Neutrophils
conversionNote: Percent ranges are unchanged; absolute counts /µL ÷ 1000 = ×10⁹/L
notes: Neutropenia: ANC <1500. Severe neutropenia: ANC <500.

name: Lymphocytes
conversionNote: Percent ranges are unchanged; absolute counts /µL ÷ 1000 = ×10⁹/L
notes: Elevated in viral infections (EBV, CMV), lymphocytic leukemia.

name: Monocytes
conversionNote: Percent ranges are unchanged; absolute counts /µL ÷ 1000 = ×10⁹/L
notes: Elevated in TB, fungal infections, inflammatory bowel disease.

name: Eosinophils
conversionNote: Percent ranges are unchanged; absolute counts /µL ÷ 1000 = ×10⁹/L
notes: Eosinophilia in parasitic infections, allergies, asthma, Addison's disease.

name: Basophils
conversionNote: Percent ranges are unchanged; absolute counts /µL ÷ 1000 = ×10⁹/L
notes: Basophilia seen in CML, polycythemia vera, hypothyroidism.

name: Platelets
notes: Thrombocytopenia (<150,000): ITP, TTP, HUS. Thrombocytosis (>400,000): reactive, essential thrombocythemia.

name: Mean Corpuscular Volume
conversionNote: Same numeric values in both systems (fL)
notes: Microcytic (<80): iron deficiency, thalassemia. Macrocytic (>100): B12/folate deficiency, liver disease.

name: Mean Corpuscular Hemoglobin
conversionNote: Same numeric values in both systems (pg)
notes: Parallel to MCV: low in microcytic, high in macrocytic anemia.

name: Mean Corpuscular Hemoglobin Concentration
notes: Elevated in hereditary spherocytosis. Decreased in iron deficiency, thalassemia.

name: Red Cell Distribution Width
conversionNote: Same numeric values in both systems (%)
notes: Elevated RDW indicates anisocytosis (iron deficiency, mixed anemia). Normal RDW in thalassemia trait.

name: Sodium
conversionNote: mEq/L and mmol/L are numerically equivalent for sodium
notes: Hyponatremia (<136): SIADH, heart failure, cirrhosis. Hypernatremia (>145): DI, dehydration.

name: Potassium
conversionNote: mEq/L and mmol/L are numerically equivalent for potassium
notes: Hypokalemia (<3.5): vomiting, diuretics, Conn's. Hyperkalemia (>5.0): renal failure, Addison's, ACE inhibitors.

name: Chloride
conversionNote: mEq/L and mmol/L are numerically equivalent for chloride
notes: Low in vomiting/metabolic alkalosis. High in diarrhea/metabolic acidosis.

name: Bicarbonate
conversionNote: mEq/L and mmol/L are numerically equivalent for bicarbonate
notes: Low in metabolic acidosis. High in metabolic alkalosis.

name: Blood Urea Nitrogen
notes: BUN:Creatinine ratio >20 suggests pre-renal azotemia. Elevated in renal failure, GI bleed.

name: Creatinine
notes: Doubles for every 50% reduction in GFR. Lower in pregnancy.

name: Glucose (Fasting)
notes: Fasting ≥8 hours. Diabetes: confirmed on two separate occasions.

name: Random Glucose
notes: Random ≥200 + symptoms = diabetes without confirmatory test needed.

name: Calcium
notes: Correct for albumin: add 0.8 mg/dL for each 1 g/dL albumin below 4. Ionized Ca: 4.5–5.6 mg/dL (1.12–1.40 mmol/L).

name: Magnesium
notes: Hypomagnesemia causes refractory hypokalemia and hypocalcemia. Used in eclampsia.

name: Phosphate
notes: Hyperphosphatemia in renal failure. Hypophosphatemia in rickets, hyperparathyroidism, refeeding syndrome.

name: Total Protein
notes: Decreased in malnutrition, liver disease, nephrotic syndrome.

name: Albumin
notes: Hypoalbuminemia: malnutrition, liver disease, nephrotic syndrome, inflammation.

name: Aspartate Aminotransferase
conversionNote: U/L and IU/L are used equivalently
notes: Present in liver, heart, muscle, kidney. AST:ALT >2:1 suggests alcoholic liver disease.

name: Alanine Aminotransferase
conversionNote: U/L and IU/L are used equivalently
notes: More liver-specific than AST. Elevated in NAFLD, viral hepatitis, drug-induced liver injury.

name: Alkaline Phosphatase
conversionNote: U/L and IU/L are used equivalently
notes: Elevated in cholestasis, bone disease (Paget's, metastases), pregnancy.

name: Gamma-Glutamyl Transferase
conversionNote: U/L and IU/L are used equivalently
notes: Sensitive for alcohol use and hepatobiliary disease. Not elevated in bone disease (unlike ALP).

name: Total Bilirubin
notes: Jaundice visible >2.5 mg/dL. Elevated in hemolysis, hepatic disease, cholestasis.

name: Direct Bilirubin
notes: Elevated in obstructive jaundice, hepatocellular disease, Dubin-Johnson, Rotor syndrome.

name: Indirect Bilirubin
notes: Elevated in hemolytic anemia, Gilbert syndrome, Crigler-Najjar syndrome.

name: Total Cholesterol
notes: Fasting not required for total cholesterol measurement alone.

name: LDL Cholesterol
notes: LDL <70 mg/dL for very high cardiovascular risk patients on statins.

name: HDL Cholesterol
notes: HDL >60 is a negative risk factor for CAD.

name: Triglycerides
notes: Requires fasting 8–12 hours. Elevated in pancreatitis at >1000 mg/dL.

name: Thyroid Stimulating Hormone
conversionNote: Same numeric values in both systems
notes: Best single test for thyroid function. Low TSH → hyperthyroidism. High TSH → hypothyroidism.

name: Free T4
notes: Active form of thyroid hormone. Decreased in hypothyroidism, increased in hyperthyroidism.

name: Free T3
notes: Most biologically active thyroid hormone. Useful in diagnosing T3 toxicosis.

name: Total T4
notes: Affected by protein-binding changes (TBG). Elevated in pregnancy, OCP use.

name: Total T3
notes: Elevated in T3 toxicosis. Low in sick euthyroid syndrome.

name: Prothrombin Time
conversionNote: Same numeric values in both systems
notes: Tests extrinsic pathway (factors VII, X, V, II, I). Prolonged in warfarin use, liver disease.

name: International Normalized Ratio
notes: Standardized measure of PT. INR >1.5 indicates coagulopathy. INR >5 = bleeding risk.

name: Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time
conversionNote: Same numeric values in both systems
notes: Tests intrinsic pathway. Prolonged in heparin therapy, hemophilia A/B.

name: Bleeding Time
conversionNote: Same numeric values in both systems
notes: Tests platelet function. Prolonged in thrombocytopenia, von Willebrand disease, aspirin use.

name: D-dimer
notes: High sensitivity, low specificity. Negative D-dimer rules out DVT/PE at low/moderate pre-test probability.

name: Fibrinogen
notes: Decreased in DIC, liver disease. Acute phase reactant — elevated in inflammation.

name: Blood pH
notes: Acidosis: pH <7.35. Alkalosis: pH >7.45. Critical: <7.20 or >7.60.

name: Arterial Oxygen Partial Pressure
notes: Hypoxemia: PaO2 <80 mmHg. Normal PaO2 ≈ 100 – (age/3).

name: Arterial Carbon Dioxide Partial Pressure
notes: Hypocapnia (<35): hyperventilation. Hypercapnia (>45): hypoventilation, COPD.

name: Oxygen Saturation
conversionNote: Same numeric values in both systems (%)
notes: SpO2 <90% (PaO2 <60) = clinically significant hypoxemia requiring intervention.

name: Anion Gap
conversionNote: mEq/L and mmol/L are numerically equivalent for monovalent ions
notes: High AG metabolic acidosis: MUDPILES (Methanol, Uremia, DKA, Propylene glycol, INH, Lactic acidosis, Ethylene glycol, Salicylates).

name: Glycated Hemoglobin
conversionNote: SI uses IFCC reporting in mmol/mol
notes: Reflects average blood glucose over 2–3 months. Not valid in hemolytic anemia, hemoglobinopathies.

name: Oral Glucose Tolerance Test
notes: Standard dose: 75 g glucose. Gold standard for diagnosing GDM.

name: Serum Iron
notes: Low in iron deficiency anemia, ACD. High in hemochromatosis.

name: Ferritin
conversionNote: ng/mL and µg/L are numerically equivalent
notes: Best indicator of iron stores. Low (<12) = iron deficiency. High in hemochromatosis, inflammation.

name: Total Iron Binding Capacity
notes: Elevated in iron deficiency. Decreased in ACD, hemochromatosis, liver disease.

name: Transferrin Saturation
conversionNote: Same numeric values in both systems (%)
notes: Low (<20%) in iron deficiency. High (>50%) in hemochromatosis.

name: Troponin I
conversionNote: ng/mL and µg/L are numerically equivalent
notes: Rises 3–6 hrs after MI, peaks 12–24 hrs, remains elevated 7–10 days.

name: Troponin T
conversionNote: ng/mL and µg/L are numerically equivalent
notes: Similar kinetics to Troponin I. hs-TnT: <14 ng/L (99th percentile).

name: CK-MB
conversionNote: ng/mL and µg/L are numerically equivalent
notes: Rises 4–8 hrs, peaks 12–24 hrs, returns to normal in 48–72 hrs.

name: B-type Natriuretic Peptide
conversionNote: pg/mL and ng/L are numerically equivalent
notes: BNP <100 makes heart failure unlikely. BNP >400 strongly suggests HF.

name: NT-proBNP
conversionNote: pg/mL and ng/L are numerically equivalent
notes: Longer half-life than BNP. Cut-off: <125 pg/mL rules out HF.

name: C-Reactive Protein
conversionNote: Conventional CRP may be reported in mg/dL; hs-CRP ranges are already in mg/L
notes: Acute phase reactant. Used in sepsis evaluation and cardiovascular risk stratification.

name: Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate
conversionNote: Same numeric values in both systems
notes: Nonspecific. Very high (>100) in giant cell arteritis, multiple myeloma, metastatic cancer.

name: Uric Acid
notes: Hyperuricemia → gout, kidney stones. Hypouricemia in Fanconi syndrome.

name: Lactate Dehydrogenase
conversionNote: U/L and IU/L are used equivalently
notes: Elevated in hemolysis, MI, PE, liver disease, lymphoma, megaloblastic anemia.

name: Amylase
conversionNote: U/L and IU/L are used equivalently
notes: Elevated >3× ULN in acute pancreatitis. Normalizes faster than lipase.

name: Lipase
conversionNote: U/L and IU/L are used equivalently
notes: More specific for pancreatitis than amylase. Remains elevated longer.

name: Vitamin B12
notes: Deficiency (<200): megaloblastic anemia, subacute combined degeneration of spinal cord.

name: Folate
notes: Deficiency causes megaloblastic anemia. Crucial in periconception period to prevent neural tube defects.

name: Vitamin D
notes: 25-OH-D is the best marker of vitamin D status. Deficiency causes rickets (children), osteomalacia (adults).

name: Urine Protein
conversionNote: Same numeric values in both systems
notes: Spot urine protein:creatinine ratio >3.5 = nephrotic range.

name: Urine Specific Gravity
notes: Fixed SG 1.010 (isosthenuria) suggests renal tubular damage.
